title: Scale Drawings
seo_title: Grade 7 Scale Drawings Worksheets: Maps, Models, Scale Factor and Area
standard_text: Solve problems involving scale drawings of geometric figures, including computing actual lengths and areas from a scale drawing and reproducing a scale drawing at a different scale.
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 scale drawings worksheets: what a scale means, real lengths from a drawing, drawing lengths from real ones, scale factor, real areas, redrawing at a new scale, and map and model word problems. 100 practice questions with an answer key.
key_big: Drawing to real life: multiply by the scale. Real life to drawing: divide.
key_sub: With a scale of 1 cm : 3 m, 6 cm on the drawing is 18 m. Areas grow by the scale factor squared.
body_html:
What a scale tells you

A scale compares a length on a drawing or map with the real length. The scale 1 cm : 3 m means every 1 cm on the drawing stands for 3 m in real life.

Going fromDo thisExample (1 cm : 3 m)
Drawing → realmultiply6 cm × 3 = 18 m
Real → drawingdivide12 m ÷ 3 = 4 cm
Areamultiply by the scale factor squaredlengths × 3, so area × 9
Example

A map scale is 1 in. : 15 miles. Two towns are 3.5 in. apart. How far apart are they?

3.5 × 15 = 52.5.

Answer: 52.5 miles

Example

A garden is drawn 3 cm by 2 cm with 1 cm : 5 m. What is its real area?

Real sides: 15 m and 10 m.

Area = 15 × 10 = 150 m².

Answer: 150 m²

Common mistakes

  • Dividing when you should multiply: from the drawing to real life, multiply.
  • Scaling area like length: if lengths are 5 times as long, the area is 25 times as large, not 5.
  • Mixing units: change 1 cm : 1 m to 1 cm : 100 cm before finding the scale factor.

faq.a: A drawing of a real object where every length is multiplied or divided by the same number. A map and a floor plan are scale drawings.

faq.q: How do I find a real length from a scale drawing?
faq.a: Multiply the drawing length by the real length that 1 unit stands for. With 1 in. : 4 ft, 3 in. on the drawing is 3 × 4 = 12 ft.

faq.q: How do I find the real area?
faq.a: Find the real lengths first, then multiply. Or multiply the drawing's area by the scale factor squared.

faq.q: How do I redraw at a different scale?
faq.a: Find the real length with the old scale, then divide by the new scale. 6 cm at 1 cm : 2 m is 12 m; at 1 cm : 4 m it is 3 cm.

items.q: What does the scale 1 inch : 20 feet mean?
c: Every 1 inch on the drawing stands for 20 feet in real life.
The real object is 1 inch long.
Every 20 inches on the drawing stand for 1 foot.
items.e: A scale compares a length on the drawing (first) with the real length (second).

items.q: What does the scale 1 cm : 5 km mean?
c: Every 1 cm on the map stands for 5 km in real life.
The map shows 1 km in all.
Every 5 cm on the map stand for 1 km.
items.e: A scale compares a length on the drawing (first) with the real length (second).

items.q: What does the scale 1 : 50 mean?
c: The real object is 50 times as large as the drawing.
The drawing is 50 times as large as the real object.
The real object is 51 times as large.
items.e: A scale compares a length on the drawing (first) with the real length (second).

items.q: A scale is 1 in. : 4 ft. How many feet does 1 inch stand for?
items.e: Divide: 4 ÷ 1 = 4 ft for each 1 in.

items.q: A scale is 2 cm : 10 m. How many meters does 1 centimeter stand for?
items.e: Divide: 10 ÷ 2 = 5 m for each 1 cm.

items.q: A scale is 1 cm : 25 km. How many kilometers does 1 centimeter stand for?
items.e: Divide: 25 ÷ 1 = 25 km for each 1 cm.

items.q: A scale is 3 in. : 15 ft. How many feet does 1 inch stand for?
items.e: Divide: 15 ÷ 3 = 5 ft for each 1 in.

items.q: A scale is 1 cm : 2.5 m. How many meters does 1 centimeter stand for?
items.e: Divide: 2.5 ÷ 1 = 2.5 m for each 1 cm.

items.q: Which scale is the same as 1 in. : 2 ft?
items.e: Multiply both parts by the same number. 1 in. : 2 ft × the same factor gives 2 in. : 4 ft.

items.q: Which scale is the same as 1 cm : 4 m?
items.e: Multiply both parts by the same number. 1 cm : 4 m × the same factor gives 3 cm : 12 m.

items.q: Which scale is the same as 1 in. : 6 ft?
items.e: Multiply both parts by the same number. 1 in. : 6 ft × the same factor gives 5 in. : 30 ft.

items.q: Which scale is the same as 2 cm : 5 m?
items.e: Multiply both parts by the same number. 2 cm : 5 m × the same factor gives 6 cm : 15 m.

items.q: What is the scale factor (real ÷ drawing, in the same units) for the scale 1 cm : 1 m?
items.e: Use the same units: 1 m = 100 cm. Real ÷ drawing = 100, so the real object is 100 times as large.

items.q: What is the scale factor (real ÷ drawing, in the same units) for the scale 1 in. : 1 ft?
items.e: Use the same units: 1 ft = 12 in. Real ÷ drawing = 12, so the real object is 12 times as large.

items.q: What is the scale factor (real ÷ drawing, in the same units) for the scale 1 cm : 2 m?
items.e: Use the same units: 2 m = 200 cm. Real ÷ drawing = 200, so the real object is 200 times as large.

items.q: What is the scale factor (real ÷ drawing, in the same units) for the scale 1 in. : 1 yd?
items.e: Use the same units: 1 yd = 36 in. Real ÷ drawing = 36, so the real object is 36 times as large.

items.q: What is the scale factor (real ÷ drawing, in the same units) for the scale 5 mm : 1 m?
items.e: Use the same units: 1 m = 1,000 mm, and 1,000 ÷ 5 = 200. Real ÷ drawing = 200, so the real object is 200 times as large.

items.q: What is the scale factor (real ÷ drawing, in the same units) for the scale 1 in. : 5 ft?
items.e: Use the same units: 5 ft = 60 in. Real ÷ drawing = 60, so the real object is 60 times as large.

items.q: What is the scale factor (real ÷ drawing, in the same units) for the scale 1 cm : 50 cm?
items.e: Use the same units: both are in cm. Real ÷ drawing = 50, so the real object is 50 times as large.

items.q: What is the scale factor (real ÷ drawing, in the same units) for the scale 2 in. : 1 ft?
items.e: Use the same units: 1 ft = 12 in., and 12 ÷ 2 = 6. Real ÷ drawing = 6, so the real object is 6 times as large.

sets.title: From the drawing to real life

items.q: A drawing uses the scale 1 in. : 4 ft. A line on the drawing is 3 in. long. How long is it in real life?
items.e: Each 1 in. stands for 4 ft. 3 × 4 = 12 ft.

items.q: A drawing uses the scale 1 cm : 10 m. A line on the drawing is 5 cm long. How long is it in real life?
items.e: Each 1 cm stands for 10 m. 5 × 10 = 50 m.

items.q: A drawing uses the scale 1 in. : 8 ft. A line on the drawing is 2.5 in. long. How long is it in real life?
items.e: Each 1 in. stands for 8 ft. 2.5 × 8 = 20 ft.

items.q: A drawing uses the scale 2 cm : 5 m. A line on the drawing is 7 cm long. How long is it in real life?
items.e: Each 2 cm stands for 5 m, so each 1 cm stands for 2.5 m. 7 × 2.5 = 17.5 m.

items.q: A drawing uses the scale 1 cm : 25 km. A line on the drawing is 4 cm long. How long is it in real life?
items.e: Each 1 cm stands for 25 km. 4 × 25 = 100 km.

items.q: A drawing uses the scale 1 in. : 2 ft. A line on the drawing is 6.5 in. long. How long is it in real life?
items.e: Each 1 in. stands for 2 ft. 6.5 × 2 = 13 ft.

items.q: A drawing uses the scale 3 cm : 10 m. A line on the drawing is 9 cm long. How long is it in real life?
items.e: Each 3 cm stands for 10 m, so each 1 cm stands for 3 13 m. 9 × 3 13 = 30 m.

items.q: A drawing uses the scale 1 cm : 1.5 m. A line on the drawing is 12 cm long. How long is it in real life?
items.e: Each 1 cm stands for 1.5 m. 12 × 1.5 = 18 m.

items.q: A drawing uses the scale 1 in. : 6 ft. A line on the drawing is 4.5 in. long. How long is it in real life?
items.e: Each 1 in. stands for 6 ft. 4.5 × 6 = 27 ft.

items.q: A drawing uses the scale 1 cm : 50 km. A line on the drawing is 8 cm long. How long is it in real life?
items.e: Each 1 cm stands for 50 km. 8 × 50 = 400 km.

items.q: A drawing uses the scale 4 cm : 3 m. A line on the drawing is 10 cm long. How long is it in real life?
items.e: Each 4 cm stands for 3 m, so each 1 cm stands for 0.75 m. 10 × 0.75 = 7.5 m.

items.q: A drawing uses the scale 1 in. : 12 ft. A line on the drawing is 1.5 in. long. How long is it in real life?
items.e: Each 1 in. stands for 12 ft. 1.5 × 12 = 18 ft.

items.q: The drawing of a garden uses the scale 1 cm : 2 m. How long is the real garden (the longer side)?
The drawing of a garden uses the scale 1 cm : 3 m. How long is the real garden (the longer side)?
The drawing of a garden uses the scale 1 cm : 4 m. How long is the real garden (the longer side)?
The drawing of a garden uses the scale 1 cm : 5 m. How long is the real garden (the longer side)?
A room is drawn with the scale 1 cm : 3 m. What is the real perimeter of the room?
items.e: Real sides: 18 m and 12 m. Perimeter = 2 × (18 + 12) = 60 m.

items.q: A room is drawn with the scale 1 cm : 4 m. What is the real perimeter of the room?
items.e: Real sides: 20 m and 8 m. Perimeter = 2 × (20 + 8) = 56 m.

items.q: A room is drawn with the scale 1 cm : 6 m. What is the real perimeter of the room?
items.e: Real sides: 18 m and 18 m. Perimeter = 2 × (18 + 18) = 72 m.

items.q: A room is drawn with the scale 1 cm : 2 m. What is the real perimeter of the room?
items.e: Real sides: 16 m and 6 m. Perimeter = 2 × (16 + 6) = 44 m.

sets.title: From real life to the drawing

items.q: A map uses the scale 1 in. : 4 ft. The real distance is 20 ft. How long is it on the map?
items.e: Divide the real length by 4 ft per in.: 20 ÷ 4 = 5 in.

items.q: A map uses the scale 1 cm : 5 m. The real distance is 45 m. How long is it on the map?
items.e: Divide the real length by 5 m per cm: 45 ÷ 5 = 9 cm.

items.q: A map uses the scale 1 in. : 6 ft. The real distance is 36 ft. How long is it on the map?
items.e: Divide the real length by 6 ft per in.: 36 ÷ 6 = 6 in.

items.q: A map uses the scale 1 cm : 25 km. The real distance is 150 km. How long is it on the map?
items.e: Divide the real length by 25 km per cm: 150 ÷ 25 = 6 cm.

items.q: A map uses the scale 2 cm : 3 m. The real distance is 18 m. How long is it on the map?
items.e: Divide the real length by 1.5 m per cm: 18 ÷ 1.5 = 12 cm.

items.q: A map uses the scale 1 in. : 20 ft. The real distance is 70 ft. How long is it on the map?
items.e: Divide the real length by 20 ft per in.: 70 ÷ 20 = 3.5 in.

items.q: A map uses the scale 1 in. : 8 ft. The real distance is 12 ft. How long is it on the map?
items.e: Divide the real length by 8 ft per in.: 12 ÷ 8 = 1.5 in.

items.q: A map uses the scale 1 cm : 2 m. The real distance is 9 m. How long is it on the map?
items.e: Divide the real length by 2 m per cm: 9 ÷ 2 = 4.5 cm.

items.q: A map uses the scale 1 cm : 40 km. The real distance is 240 km. How long is it on the map?
items.e: Divide the real length by 40 km per cm: 240 ÷ 40 = 6 cm.

items.q: A map uses the scale 1 in. : 10 ft. The real distance is 35 ft. How long is it on the map?
items.e: Divide the real length by 10 ft per in.: 35 ÷ 10 = 3.5 in.

items.q: A map uses the scale 3 cm : 9 m. The real distance is 27 m. How long is it on the map?
items.e: Divide the real length by 3 m per cm: 27 ÷ 3 = 9 cm.

items.q: A map uses the scale 1 cm : 10 m. The real distance is 55 m. How long is it on the map?
items.e: Divide the real length by 10 m per cm: 55 ÷ 10 = 5.5 cm.

sets.title: Area, finding the scale and redrawing

items.q: A rectangle on a drawing is 3 cm by 2 cm. The scale is 1 cm : 5 m. What is the real area?
items.e: Real sides: 15 m and 10 m. Area = 15 × 10 = 150 m². Not 30 m²: the area grows by 5² = 25, not 5.

items.q: A rectangle on a drawing is 4 cm by 3 cm. The scale is 1 cm : 2 m. What is the real area?
items.e: Real sides: 8 m and 6 m. Area = 8 × 6 = 48 m². Not 24 m²: the area grows by 2² = 4, not 2.

items.q: A rectangle on a drawing is 6 cm by 5 cm. The scale is 1 cm : 10 m. What is the real area?
items.e: Real sides: 60 m and 50 m. Area = 60 × 50 = 3000 m². Not 300 m²: the area grows by 10² = 100, not 10.

items.q: A rectangle on a drawing is 5 cm by 2 cm. The scale is 1 cm : 4 m. What is the real area?
items.e: Real sides: 20 m and 8 m. Area = 20 × 8 = 160 m². Not 40 m²: the area grows by 4² = 16, not 4.

items.q: A rectangle on a drawing is 8 cm by 3 cm. The scale is 1 cm : 3 m. What is the real area?
items.e: Real sides: 24 m and 9 m. Area = 24 × 9 = 216 m². Not 72 m²: the area grows by 3² = 9, not 3.

items.q: A rectangle on a drawing is 2 cm by 2 cm. The scale is 1 cm : 25 m. What is the real area?
items.e: Real sides: 50 m and 50 m. Area = 50 × 50 = 2500 m². Not 100 m²: the area grows by 25² = 625, not 25.

items.q: A drawing uses a scale factor of 3. How many times as large is the real area as the drawing's area?
items.e: Each length is 3 times as long, so the area is 3 × 3 = 9 times as large.

items.q: A drawing uses a scale factor of 5. How many times as large is the real area as the drawing's area?
items.e: Each length is 5 times as long, so the area is 5 × 5 = 25 times as large.

items.q: A drawing uses a scale factor of 10. How many times as large is the real area as the drawing's area?
items.e: Each length is 10 times as long, so the area is 10 × 10 = 100 times as large.

items.q: A drawing uses a scale factor of 4. How many times as large is the real area as the drawing's area?
items.e: Each length is 4 times as long, so the area is 4 × 4 = 16 times as large.

items.q: A drawing uses the scale 1 cm : 2 m. A wall is 6 cm long on it. You redraw it with the scale 1 cm : 4 m. How long is the wall on the new drawing?
items.e: Real length: 6 × 2 = 12 m. New drawing: 12 ÷ 4 = 3 cm.

items.q: A drawing uses the scale 1 cm : 5 m. A wall is 10 cm long on it. You redraw it with the scale 1 cm : 2 m. How long is the wall on the new drawing?
items.e: Real length: 10 × 5 = 50 m. New drawing: 50 ÷ 2 = 25 cm.

items.q: A drawing uses the scale 1 cm : 3 m. A wall is 8 cm long on it. You redraw it with the scale 1 cm : 6 m. How long is the wall on the new drawing?
items.e: Real length: 8 × 3 = 24 m. New drawing: 24 ÷ 6 = 4 cm.

items.q: A drawing uses the scale 1 cm : 10 m. A wall is 4 cm long on it. You redraw it with the scale 1 cm : 5 m. How long is the wall on the new drawing?
items.e: Real length: 4 × 10 = 40 m. New drawing: 40 ÷ 5 = 8 cm.

items.q: A drawing uses the scale 1 cm : 2 m. A wall is 9 cm long on it. You redraw it with the scale 1 cm : 3 m. How long is the wall on the new drawing?
items.e: Real length: 9 × 2 = 18 m. New drawing: 18 ÷ 3 = 6 cm.

items.q: A drawing uses the scale 1 cm : 4 m. A wall is 12 cm long on it. You redraw it with the scale 1 cm : 8 m. How long is the wall on the new drawing?
items.e: Real length: 12 × 4 = 48 m. New drawing: 48 ÷ 8 = 6 cm.

items.q: A 4 in. line on a drawing stands for 20 ft. What is the scale written as 1 in. : ?
items.e: 20 ÷ 4 = 5, so the scale is 1 in. : 5 ft.

items.q: A 6 cm line on a drawing stands for 30 m. What is the scale written as 1 cm : ?
items.e: 30 ÷ 6 = 5, so the scale is 1 cm : 5 m.

items.q: A 3 in. line on a drawing stands for 45 ft. What is the scale written as 1 in. : ?
items.e: 45 ÷ 3 = 15, so the scale is 1 in. : 15 ft.

items.q: A 5 cm line on a drawing stands for 2 km. What is the scale written as 1 cm : ?
items.e: 2 ÷ 5 = 0.4, so the scale is 1 cm : 0.4 km.

sets.title: Word problems: maps, models and plans

items.q: On a map, 1 inch = 15 miles. Two towns are 3.5 inches apart. How far apart are they?
A map scale is 1 cm : 50 km. Two cities are 375 km apart. How far apart are they on the map?
A model car is built at a scale of 1 : 24. The model is 7.5 inches long. How long is the real car in feet?
A blueprint uses 14 inch = 1 foot. A wall is 3 12 inches long on it. How long is the real wall?
items.e: 3 12 ÷ 14 = 14 feet.

items.q: A dollhouse uses a scale of 1 inch : 1 foot. A real door is 7 feet tall. How tall is the dollhouse door?
items.e: 1 inch for each foot: 7 feet → 7 inches.

items.q: A map uses 2 cm : 25 km. A road is 9 cm long on the map. How long is the real road?
A school is 120 m long. On a plan it is 24 cm long. What is the scale (1 cm : ? m)?
A park is drawn 8 cm by 5 cm with scale 1 cm : 20 m. What is the real area?
A photo 4 in. by 6 in. is enlarged with scale factor 2.5. What are the new length and width? Give the longer side.
The Statue of Liberty is about 151 ft tall. A souvenir uses the scale 1 in. : 25 ft. About how tall is the souvenir?
An ant is 6 mm long. In a drawing it is 9 cm long. What is the scale factor?
items.e: 9 cm = 90 mm. 90 ÷ 6 = 15. The drawing is 15 times as large.

items.q: A soccer field is 100 m by 64 m. You draw it with 1 cm : 4 m. What is the drawing's length?
A map scale is 1 in. : 40 mi. A trip is 260 mi. How many inches is it on the map?
A tiny cell is 0.02 mm wide. A picture shows it 3 cm wide. What is the scale factor?
A room on a plan is 5 in. by 4 in. The scale is 1 in. : 3 ft. Carpet costs $4 per square foot. What does carpet for the room cost?
Two scale drawings show the same 30 m wall. Drawing A uses 1 cm : 2 m and drawing B uses 1 cm : 5 m. How much longer is the wall on drawing A?
A model airplane has a wingspan of 18 in. The scale is 1 : 48. What is the real wingspan in feet?
On a map, 3 cm stands for 12 km. A lake is 7 cm across on the map. How wide is the real lake?
A square patio is drawn 3 in. on each side. The scale is 1 in. : 4 ft. What is the patio's real area?
items.e: Real side: 12 ft. Area = 12 × 12 = 144 ft².

items.q: A poster enlarges a 2 cm stamp to 50 cm. What is the scale factor?
